title: GPU price hikes, Azure's vanishing price lock, and AI as its own negotiation line
summary: AWS renames EDP to PPA and raises GPU Capacity Block prices 20%. Azure's 3-year EA price lock does not carry over to MCA-E or CSP, sharpening the cost of migrating without negotiating a bridge. Vertex AI emerges as the least-scrutinized line item in Google Cloud deals.
highlights: EC2 GPU Capacity Block prices up ~20% effective July 1 — second hike this year
Azure's EA price lock doesn't transfer to MCA-E or CSP — the real cost of migrating off EA
Vertex AI runs 18-32% below published rates inside a CUD, 38-52% for Provisioned Throughput
FinOps practitioners now pulled into M&A due diligence, not just cost reviews

title: EA-to-MCA-E migration, CUD scope changes, and the first Database Savings Plans
summary: Microsoft begins moving EA customers to MCA-E ahead of renewal, eliminating the Level B/C/D discount structure. Google changes CUD default scope in a way that disrupts project-level chargeback. AWS Database Savings Plans reach GA and go almost entirely unclaimed in EDP negotiations.
highlights: Clients migrating to MCA-E without negotiating are seeing 10–30% cost increases
GCP CUD scope now defaults to billing-account level for new accounts
Flex CUDs extended to cover GKE Autopilot and Cloud Run
All six tool recommendations from this issue have since shipped
